title: BET Announces Chaka Khan Humanitarian Award at the 2026 Soul Train Awards
summary: The inaugural award will be presented at the 2027 Soul Train Awards The post BET Announces Chaka Khan Humanitarian Award at the 2026 Soul Train Awards appeared first on TheWrap .
content: BET announced on Friday that it has established the Chaka Khan Humanitarian Award, a new annual honor which will recognize musicians and cultural figures who have made outstanding contributions to humanitarianism, community service and social justice. The announcement was made at the 2026 Soul Train Awards. The first award will be bestowed at next year’s 2027 Soul Train Awards. The award will honor individuals “demonstrating a longstanding commitment to creating meaningful change, particularly through efforts supporting children’s welfare, women’s empowerment and marginalized communities,” per the press release. It is named in recognition of Khan’s “enduring dedication to advocacy and service, the honor celebrates artists whose impact extends beyond music and entertainment to improve the lives of others.” “My music has given me a voice, but love has given me purpose,” the 11-time Grammy winner said at the awards show. “This award isn’t about me; it’s about all of us who believe in lifting others, holding each other up, and building a world where compassion lives. I’m grateful to everyone who walks that path and future generations to carry this forward.” Khan, affectionately known as the Queen of Funk, founded the Chaka Khan Foundation in 1999. Initially focused on autism awareness and providing resources to underserved communities, the foundation later expanded its mission to support at-risk women and children, while continuing to champion inclusive support and vocational development programs for neurodiverse populations. Friday’s Soul Train Awards also celebrated achievement in soul and R&B music, with Tyla winning R&B Song of the Year and Partynextdoor taking home the RNB X International Artist Award. Upcoming artist Elmiene won the New Soul Honor, while Durand Bernarr received the Soul Personified Honor. Tributes were also held for DJ Sam Chapman, Dolly Parton and Freddie Jackson. Khan, who also took home the Classic Soul Honor, returned to the stage to close the night with a show-stopping performance of “I’m Every Woman,” “Through the Fire” and “Chakzilla.” The post BET Announces Chaka Khan Humanitarian Award at the 2026 Soul Train Awards appeared first on TheWrap .

title: Everything to Know About Raye, the Macy’s Thanksgiving Parade Opening Act
summary: The British singer recently tied Beyonce for most Grammy nominations for a female artist in a single year The post Everything to Know About Raye, the Macy’s Thanksgiving Parade Opening Act appeared first on TheWrap .
content: Raye has been burning up the charts for over a year, but if you just discovered her talent during the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade, you’re in luck. Here’s everything you need to know about the British singer-songwriter. What is Raye’s real name? Raye was born Rachel Agatha Keen on Oct. 24, 1997 to a Swiss-German/ Ghanaian mother and English father. Her younger sisters Amma (Lauren Amma Keen) and Absolutely (Abby-Lynn Keen) are also singers. Hold old is Raye? Raye recently turned 29 years old on Oct. 24, 2026. Why is Raye famous? Before performing the opening musical number for the 2026 Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade with her sisters Amma and Absolutely, Raye had a breakout year in 2025. Although she has been performing since she was a teen and released one solo and one studio album, Raye received the Best New Artist nomination at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards in February. She was also nominated for Songwriter of the Year, Non-Classical and Best Engineered Album (Non-Classical for Algorithm). At the ceremony, she performed a medley with her fellow Best New Artist nominees, though she did not win any awards that night. One month later at the 97th Academy Awards, Raye performed Adele’s “Skyfall” as part of a James Bond tribute . In September, she released “Where Is My Husband!” (often mistakenly called “Where the Hell Is My Husband” from its lyrics). The catchy song peaked at No. 1 in her native U.K. and No. 11 in the United States and earned Raye a slew of award nominations. “Where Is My Husband!” was the lead single off her second studio album “This Music May Contain Hope” released in March 2026. The album also spawned singles “Nightingale Lane” and “Click Clack Symphony.” What Awards Has Raye Won? Following her three Grammy nominations in 2025, RAYE earned another nod in 2026 for Best Music Film for “Live at the Royal Albert Hall,” but did not win. Last month, she earned a staggering 11 nominations for the upcoming 2027 Grammys, including Album of the Year and Best Pop Vocal Album for “This Music May Contain Hope”; Record of the Year, Song of the Year and Best Pop Solo Performance for “Where Is My Husband!”; Best Pop Duo/Group Performance, Best Arrangement, Instruments and Vocals and Best Music Video for “Click Clack Symphony”; Best Dance Pop Recording for “Life Boat”; Best Traditional Pop Vocal Performance for “I Hate the Way I Look Today”; and Songwriter of the Year, Non-Classical. Her 11 nominations tie her with Beyoncé for the most Grammy nominations by a female artist in a single year. The 69th Annual Grammy Awards will be held Feb. 7, 2027, at Crypto.com Arena. Where can I find Raye online? Raye has her own official artist page and active Instagram , Tiktok and Facebook accounts. Where I can see Raye perform? In addition to the 2026 Macy’s Thanksgiving Parade, which will air live on NBC and encore later that same day, Raye is currently touring. Her next three appearances will be at the iHeart Jingle Balls in Fort Worth, Texas (Dec. 1), Los Angeles, Calif. (Dec. 4) and Rosemont, Ill. (Dec. 7). title: ‘Pride and Prejudice’ Star Reveals ‘Gorgeous’ Personal Message From Ex Mr. Darcys
summary: Lowden brings the Jane Austen character to life in Netflix's latest adaptation The post ‘Pride and Prejudice’ Star Reveals ‘Gorgeous’ Personal Message From Ex Mr. Darcys appeared first on TheWrap .
content: Jack Lowden knows it’ll take a lot to fill Mr. Darcy’s (wet) shoes , but he has the support of two previous “Pride and Prejudice” stars. The Scottish actor, best known for his role on “Slow Horses,” will play the iconic Jane Austen character in Netflix’s new adaptation , streaming Dec. 3. During a press tour for the upcoming series, Lowden revealed that he received words of support from two former and iconic Mr. Darcys: Colin Firth and Matthew Macfadyen. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Stylist Magazine (@stylistmagazine) “I got a joint email from Colin and Matthew titled ‘The audacity, sir,'” Lowden recalled to Stylist magazine. “They wished me all the best. They said welcome to the club,” he added. “It was a really gorgeous email to get when they found out I was going to play him.” “You gotta frame that or something, that’s so cool,” chimed in his costar Emma Corrin, who plays Elizabeth Bennet. “I’m going to print it out,” Lowden replied. “It’s a cool club.” Firth played Mr. Darcy in the 1995 BBC series, not to be confused with Mark Darcy, the character he played in four “Bridget Jones” movies spanning 2001 through 2025. Macfadyen brought a brooding Mr. Darcy to the big screen adaptation of “Pride & Prejudice” in 2005, opposite Keira Knightley. There have been numerous adaptations of Jane Austen’s 1813 novel including a Bollywood version called “Bride and Prejudice,” as well as a horror satire called “Pride and Prejudice and Zombies.” Netflix’s “Pride and Prejudice,” written by Dolly Alderton and also starring Olivia Colman and Rufus Sewell, arrives on the streamer Dec. 3. title: Bronson Reed, WWE Star, Dead at 38
summary: The pro wrestler, whose real name was Jermaine Haley, died due to "medical complications" per the WWE The post Bronson Reed, WWE Star, Dead at 38 appeared first on TheWrap .
content: Bronson Reed, World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE) star, has died at 38. Reed’s real name was Jermaine Haley. WWE announced his death on Friday, Nov. 27 from “medical complications.” The organization did not elaborate further. “Jermaine was a larger-than-life figure in WWE, but more importantly, a devoted family man, and a beloved colleague,” WWE said in a statement posted online. WWE is devastated to announce that Jermaine Haley, known to WWE fans as Bronson Reed, passed away earlier today. Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with Jermaine’s family, friends and fans. pic.twitter.com/5ttxdSi3kb — WWE (@WWE) November 28, 2026 “Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with Jermaine’s entire family, including his pregnant wife, Paige, their daughter, as well as his friends, co-workers and fans,” the statement continued. Bronson wrestled on the independent circuit in his native Australia before being signed by WWE in 2019, per Yahoo! Sports . He was associated with The Vision wrestling stable that includes Logan Paul. His last event was the WWE Crown Jewel in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia early this month. Reed wasn’t part of the Crown Jewel card but interfered in a match. He was tossed out of the ring by wrestler Oba Femi and onto a table. Reed reportedly sustained multiple broken and a lacerated kidney which left him hospitalized in Saudi Arabia, according to Sports Illustrated . The wrestling community was stunned by Reed’s death, and many took to social media to mourn him. I’m at a loss for words. title: John Carpenter Cheekily Accepts William Shatner’s Apology for Dissing Him at Fan Event: ‘I’m Nothing if Not Generous’
summary: The "Halloween" icon called the "Star Trek" vet a "piece of s--t" for giving him the cold shoulder at a Florida convention The post John Carpenter Cheekily Accepts William Shatner’s Apology for Dissing Him at Fan Event: ‘I’m Nothing if Not Generous’ appeared first on TheWrap .
content: John Carpenter and William Shatner were ensnared in an unlikely but brief feud this week after the “Star Trek” icon apparently snubbed the “Halloween” maestro while attending the same fan convention in Orlando, Fla. All was forgiven Friday, however, when Carpenter cheekily responded to Shatner’s public apology on his Instagram account, writing, “I’m willing to give you another chance. I’m nothing if not generous … After all, even Captain Kirk deserves a second chance at first contact.” The kerfuffle came about after Carpenter recalled on the “Dropping Names” podcast earlier this month how Shatner gave him the cold shoulder when he went to introduce himself in their shared greenroom, calling the actor a “piece of s–t” for not looking up from his phone during the encounter. “This guy, he’s sitting in the greenroom, on his phone like this [scrolling]. And I just thought, ‘Well, I’m going to go in and introduce myself.’ I said, ‘Hello, Mr. Shatner, I’m John Carpenter,’” Carpenter said. “‘Pleasure.’ Did not look up from the phone. This piece of s–t did not look up from the phone. He’s an asshole.” View this post on Instagram A post shared by John Carpenter (Official) (@johncarpenterofficial) On Friday, Shatner addressed the incident in a written and hand-signed apology on his own social media pages , explaining, “Obviously I didn’t hear you. I was probably reading a great review of one of your movies and it occupied my attention to the point where I didn’t look up.” “Next time you see me, please come over and introduce yourself, because I really don’t know what you look like and apparently you know what I look like,” he continued. “But I would enjoy saying hello to you, and this piece of s–t would confide in you his admiration.” Carpenter soon enough let bygones be bygones and accepted Shatner’s apology, but not before reemphasizing his rudeness in the moment. “I met you in Orlando, or I should say, I said hello to you and introduced myself in Orlando. You would not look me in the eye. Maybe it’s a Canadian thing,” he wrote. title: Storm Displaces Kennedy Center Tarp, Confirming Trump’s Name Was Removed
summary: The powerful storms that pummeled the Northeast revealed only JFK's name remains on the D.C. landmark The post Storm Displaces Kennedy Center Tarp, Confirming Trump’s Name Was Removed appeared first on TheWrap .
content: The powerful storms that pummeled the Northeast and postponed the Macy’s Thanksgiving Parade have had another unintended effect. On Thanksgiving, strong winds displaced the tarp-covered scaffolding in front of the John F. Kennedy Memorial Center for the Performing Arts in Washington D.C., revealing that President Trump’s name is no longer on the building. Back in December 2025, the Kennedy Center’s board of trustees — mostly handpicked by Trump — voted to add Trump’s name to the landmark, long considered a living memorial to John F. Kennedy since its groundbreaking in 1964. The following day, metal letters were added above the existing name to read The Donald J. Trump and the John F. Kennedy Memorial Center for the Performing Arts, despite protests from the public, historical preservationists and the Kennedy family. In May 2026, judge Christopher Cooper ruled that Trump’s name could not be added to the building without congressional approval, nor could it be associated with any promotional materials and signs. “Congress gave the Kennedy Center its name, and only Congress can change it,” Cooper wrote at the time, ordering the letters be removed within 14 days. Scaffolding was erected and workers were heard working, but no one actually knew if the letters were removed because a giant tarp blocked the view. However, Thursday’s nor’easter blew away that tarp, confirming Trumps name was indeed removed, as you can see in NBC 4’s post below: Most of the tarp remains attached to the scaffolding after the Thanksgiving storm. But an upper corner of the tarp detached itself and now shows the empty wall where Trump’s name used to be. https://t.co/GM6rtuQkoE — NBC4 Washington (@nbcwashington) November 27, 2026 The same board voted to close the Kennedy Center in September, citing repairs and renovations. Trump then threatened that the Center would be “ripped down” if his administration’s efforts weren’t recognized. Cooper ruled that the building could not be demolished or any new structures be built without 30 days notice. With the Center closed, the annual Kennedy Center Honors, which have recognized performing arts contributions to American culture since 1978, will be moved for the first time . The 2026 Kennedy Center Honors, recognizing Paul Anka, David Foster, Andy Garcia, David Mamet and Barbara Mandrell, will be held at Capital One Arena on Dec. 7. The 2025 ceremony, hosted by President Donald Trump, drew 3.01 million viewers on CBS, the smallest audience in the Honors’ history . The telecast was also streamed on Paramount+. Honorees included Sylvester Stallone, George Strait, Gloria Gaynor, Michael Crawford and the rock band Kiss.
